Now mentions clozapine and pituitary alternatives, but normal visual fields alone cannot exclude a small prolactinoma; the untreated hypothyroidism is the stronger supplied clue. Length/repetition exceeds the normal concise target. Acknowledges unverified evidence. The clozapine attribution is not externally checked by this agent.

C still differs from released B. Recognizes limb-threatening ischemia, but mentions possible Rutherford III alongside IIb without distinguishing the nonsalvageable category's different management. The guideline supports immediate UFH and emergency viability/revascularization assessment for salvageable ischemia; no Doppler findings establish a complete stage here. Urgent rescue can be clinically appropriate for IIb, while the unexplained III alternative is a material imprecision. No PubMed search was chosen; original key/prioritization ambiguity remains.
